text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Guntis Ulmanis expressed concerns over the political instability in the neighbouring Byelorussia which he believes may provoke a flow of illegal immigrants to Latvia.
- Presidents of Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia are meeting in Riga on Tuesday.
- The District Court of Riga has sentenced one of the leaders of the organised crime, Janis Kalva, to four year in jail.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele did not accept the amendments to the budget draft, proposed by the faction of the Democratic Party Saimnieks. The party has not as yet decided how to react.
- The party Latvia's Way denies having approved an agreement between one of its members, Yevgueny Vasilyev, and the mayor of Daugavpils, Aleksei Vidavskis.
- Fifteen candidates have applied for post of chief manager of the port of Riga. Candidates will be considered by the board of the Riga's harbours in late December.

- The Lithuanian Committee for Securities has issued a statement which warns investors against using services offered by the Latvian Rietumu Banka in Lithuania's securities market. The committee said the bank does not have the necessary licence to operate in Lithuania but Rietumu banka said the conflict originates in the complicated relations between Latvia and Lithuania.
